third_party_dependencies.name: ruff
third_party_dependencies.necessity: Pinned CI-only static checker; it is not imported by or required to run the paper product or governance verifier.

permissions_or_telemetry.network: Installation may contact the canonical package host; repository configuration grants no network operation to the checker itself.
permissions_or_telemetry.filesystem: Reads repository source and may write an ephemeral CI cache; it has no product-data role.
permissions_or_telemetry.process: Runs only as a CI lint or format-check process.
permissions_or_telemetry.telemetry: No telemetry endpoint, credential, or opt-in is configured by this repository.
permissions_or_telemetry.evidence_basis: Pinned workflow invocation and official release metadata; upstream binary behavior is outside this static verifier's proof scope.

third_party_dependencies.removal_plan: Delete the CI install and Ruff checks; retain standard-library compilation, unit, behavior, attack, and recovery checks as the minimum replacement gate.

claim_boundary.proves: For the declared repository bytes, the verifier derives Python imports, literal dynamic imports, statically visible installer commands, supported dependency configuration entries, and external GitHub Action revisions; it rejects unregistered or floating dependencies and unknown declared telemetry.
does_not_prove: absence of vulnerabilities or telemetry in the operating system, Python runtime, standard library, GitHub runner, external Actions, upstream binaries, or service providers
behavior hidden behind runtime-generated non-shell process arguments
correctness or safety of a dependency merely because its identity and review fields are registered
transitive artifacts selected by an installer unless a future enforced lock or hash installation path binds them
claim_boundary.current_expected_observation: runtime and governance Python third-party import sets are empty; the separately reported CI tool set contains only registered ruff
